title: SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Falls 9.0% on Midterm Regulation Worries (Nov 5)
summary: SPCX closed at $123.62 on Nov 5, down 9.05%, as regulatory worries after the Democratic midterm sweep and an AI selloff weighed on SpaceX stock.
body_markdown:
## Why SpaceX Stock Fell


Financial media tied the drop to the results of Tuesday's midterm elections. According to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-thursday-november-5-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-plunge-chip-stocks-melt-down-193726491.html) , SpaceX and Tesla extended their declines on Thursday over concerns about regulatory hurdles for data center buildouts in the US, with the Democratic win in Texas, where both companies are headquartered, at the center of the concern. As reported by[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/tech-stocks-plunge-ai-midterms-rcna607650) , SpaceX has recently emerged as a data center developer, and many winning Democrats pledged to slow or halt AI data center construction.


NBC News added that Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars to help elect Republican candidates, and that he and his companies now face the prospect of tighter regulation and possible state and federal investigations. Analyst Dan Ives wrote that a possible SpaceX and Tesla merger "now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027," per Yahoo Finance.


The wider selloff added to the pressure. Per NBC News, lackluster[results from Qualcomm and Arm Holdings](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/chip-earnings-selloff-qualcomm-arm-marvell/) on Wednesday night triggered the AI selloff, and the Nasdaq Composite entered correction territory. According to Yahoo Finance, Nomura's Charlie McElligott attributed the move mainly to hedge funds locking in profits before the end of the year rather than to weaker fundamentals.


## SPCX Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to[SpaceX's third-quarter 2026 results release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066482/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm) , revenue rose 161% year over year to $14.6 billion, and the company posted net income of $4.4 billion against a net loss of $1,054 million a year earlier.
- The Super Intelligence segment brought in $7,560 million, which SpaceX attributed to new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and increased Grok adoption.
- Connectivity revenue grew 69% to $5,248 million, and Starlink ended September with 13.6 million consumer subscribers, up 1.6 million from the prior quarter, per the company's[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) .


### Risks


- SpaceX's Super Intelligence segment, which reached 1.7 GW of nameplate compute by September 30, relies on data center buildouts that many winning Democrats pledged to slow or halt, per NBC News.
- Third-quarter capital expenditures reached $19,593 million, up from $6,880 million a year earlier, with $16,444 million in Super Intelligence, while NBC News reported that investors increasingly question whether AI investments will pay off.
- SpaceX's planned purchase of 800 MHz spectrum licenses for Starlink Mobile is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory and other customary closing conditions, according to the company.
